page: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-300s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled at 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is supported by 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 300 GB NVMe SSD. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25% of tested systems. Multi-core execution, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks also demonstrate average throughput. Notably, the server exhibits top-tier performance in text generation for small language models and strong performance in text generation for medium models, alongside strong image and text processing capabilities.

Given its dedicated AMD EPYC cores and high-speed NVMe storage, this server offers a balanced, compute-focused resource profile. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring dedicated CPU execution without the overhead of massive memory allocations. It is well-suited for tasks such as software compilation, medium-scale web serving, database operations, and text-based machine learning inference.
